children: Italian gambling group Lottomatica’s shares sank 10% after it offered €3 bln for Spain’s Cirsa. That probably overstates the risks of expanding outside its home market and downplays the logic of the all-share merger. And the Blackstone-backed target is hardly rich.
Full view will be published shortly.
Lottomatica on September 2 agreed to buy Spanish gambling group Cirsa for €3 billion.
Under the terms of the transaction, Lottomatica will offer 0.668 of its own shares, and a €262 million special dividend. That values Cirsa at 16.5 euros a share, or 18 euros including the dividend.
Shares in Lottomatica were down 10% at 22.22 euros each, as of 10:15 GMT on September 2.
